def-abstract-root-datum-and-its-weyl-gro.before_interface:
A **root datum** is a quadruple $(X,\Phi,X^\vee,\Phi^\vee)$ consisting of free $\mathbb Z$-modules $X,X^\vee$ of finite rank in perfect duality $\langle\ ,\ \rangle:X\times X^\vee\to\mathbb Z$, finite subsets $\Phi\subseteq X$ and $\Phi^\vee\subseteq X^\vee$, and a bijection $\alpha\mapsto\alpha^\vee$ from $\Phi$ to $\Phi^\vee$, subject to (rd1) $\langle\alpha,\alpha^\vee\rangle=2$ for all $\alpha\in\Phi$; (rd2) the reflections $s_\alpha(x)=x-\langle x,\alpha^\vee\rangle\alpha$ and $s_{\alpha^\vee}(y)=y-\langle\alpha,y\rangle\alpha^\vee$ satisfy $s_\alpha(\Phi)\subseteq\Phi$ and $s_{\alpha^\vee}(\Phi^\vee)\subseteq\Phi^\vee$; (rd3) the group $W(R)$ generated by the $s_\alpha$ acting on $X$ is finite. The root datum is **reduced** if $\mathbb Q\alpha\cap\Phi=\{\pm\alpha\}$ for every $\alpha\in\Phi$. The group $W(R)$ is the **Weyl group**, $\Phi$ the root system and $\Phi^\vee$ the coroot system; $W(R)$ acts dually on $X^\vee$ by the $s_{\alpha^\vee}$, and $s_\alpha$ fixes the hyperplane $\langle\ ,\alpha^\vee\rangle=0$. For $V_{\mathbb R}=X\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb R$, the **Weyl chambers** are the connected components of $V_{\mathbb R}\smallsetminus\bigcup_{\alpha\in\Phi}\{x:\langle x,\alpha^\vee\rangle=0\}$, and a **base** is a linearly independent subset $\Delta\subseteq\Phi$ such that every root is a $\mathbb Z$-combination of $\Delta$ with all coefficients of one sign. A root datum is **semisimple** if $Z\Phi$ has finite index in $X$.

The reflection $s_\alpha$ depends only on the pair $(\alpha,\alpha^\vee)$: it fixes the hyperplane $\langle\ ,\alpha^\vee\rangle=0$, sends $\alpha$ to $-\alpha$ by (rd1), and is determined by those two conditions on the rational direct sum $\mathbb Q\alpha\oplus\ker(\langle\ ,\alpha^\vee\rangle:X\otimes\mathbb Q\to\mathbb Q)$. The lattice form above is related to the Euclidean root-system theory of [[def-weyl-group-of-a-root-system]] and [[def-positive-system-and-base-of-simple-roots]] through a $W$-invariant form on $V_{\mathbb R}$, but no choice of invariant inner product belongs to the definition; the lattice form, not the Euclidean one, is what is attached to a split reductive group in [[lem-character-and-cocharacter-lattices-of-a-split-torus]].

An **isomorphism of root data** $R=(X,\Phi,X^\vee,\Phi^\vee)\to R_1=(X_1,\Phi_1,X_1^\vee,\Phi_1^\vee)$ is a pair of $\mathbb Z$-linear isomorphisms $f:X\to X_1$ and $f^\vee:X_1^\vee\to X^\vee$ that are transpose to one another, $\langle f(x),y_1\rangle=\langle x,f^\vee(y_1)\rangle$ for all $x\in X$, $y_1\in X_1^\vee$, and that carry $\Phi$ bijectively onto $\Phi_1$ with $f(\alpha)^\vee=f^\vee{} ^{-1}(\alpha^\vee)$ for every $\alpha\in\Phi$. Composites of isomorphisms are isomorphisms, with the evident inverses, so root data form a category whose isomorphisms are these pairs; this is the notion of isomorphism used when separating the root data of SL_2 and PGL_2.

def-parabolic-subgroup-of-an-affine-alge.before_interface:
Let $G$ be a smooth affine algebraic group of finite type over $k$ ([[def-group-scheme-over-a-field]], [[def-smooth-morphism-schemes]], [[def-affine-scheme]]). A closed subgroup scheme $P\subseteq G$ is a **parabolic subgroup** if the fppf quotient $G/P$ is representable and proper over $k$, equivalently if $G/P$ is complete ([[thm-homogeneous-space-for-smooth-affine-group]], [[def-proper-morphism]], [[def-complete-variety]]). The **unipotent radical** $R_u(P)\subseteq P$ is the largest smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup ([[def-unipotent-algebraic-group]]), the **radical** $R(P)$ is the largest smooth connected normal solvable subgroup ([[def-derived-subgroup-and-solvable-algebraic-group]], [[def-radical-and-unipotent-radical-of-an-algebraic-group]]), and a **Levi subgroup** of $P$ is a smooth closed subgroup $L\subseteq P$ such that the multiplication map $L\ltimes R_u(P)\to P$ is an isomorphism. Borel subgroups and the equivalence 'parabolic iff, over $k^{\mathrm a}$, contains a Borel subgroup' are treated on this page in [[thm-solvable-subgroups-and-the-radical-as-borel-intersection]] and [[def-borel-subgroup-and-maximal-torus]].

The conditional proper-quotient definition above uses no choice principle. Assume the Axiom of Choice for the following supplemental representability and structural assertions ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Representability of $G/P$ is a theorem for smooth affine $G$ and closed $P$ ([[thm-homogeneous-space-for-smooth-affine-group]]); properness of a representable quotient is equivalent to completeness by definition, which is the form used in the propositions below. The definition does not assume $P$ smooth or connected; in a smooth connected affine group such a parabolic is connected and self-normalizing by [[thm-solvable-subgroups-and-the-radical-as-borel-intersection]]. Smooth parabolic subgroup varieties form the class to which the standard $P_I$ and Levi classification below applies; nonsmooth Frobenius-thickened proper-quotient subgroups are retained by this general definition. The definition makes no reference to split reductive structure, so that the standard-parabolic theory can establish the equivalence for smooth subgroup varieties. In the Levi decomposition below the subgroup $L$ is required only to be smooth and closed; when $P$ is smooth, its unipotent radical is smooth and the product decomposition is a statement about schemes.

thm-chevalley-centralizer-radical-and-re.before_interface: Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited from the named suppliers. Let $G$ be a smooth connected affine group variety over an algebraically closed field $k$ and let $T$ be a maximal torus.
